answer: Stake-weighted attestations with slashing are one concrete Sybil defense. Each agent locks collateral to earn a vote, and voting power follows stake, not headcount, so splitting one wallet into a thousand fakes buys no extra influence. A validator caught vouching for a phantom peer loses its bond and is ejected. To sway a vote, an attacker must lock more value than all honest agents combined, paying the full cost up front to reach the zenith of influence. A gale of fresh wallets changes nothing; honest agents rest on a solid mesa of forfeitable collateral that makes lying too costly.
